hints: Rewrite both double-angle terms using $\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ and $\cos2\theta=\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta$.
Substitute these into the given equation and move $2\sin^2\theta$ to the left before collecting terms.
walkthrough:
State the standard double-angle formulae for sine and cosine:
$$\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$$
$$\cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$$

Substitute these identities into the left-hand side of $\sin 2\theta + \cos 2\theta = 2\sin^2\theta$:
$$2\sin\theta\cos\theta + (\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta) = 2\sin^2\theta$$

Subtract $2\sin^2\theta$ from both sides to collect all terms on the left-hand side:
$$\cos^2\theta + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta - \sin^2\theta - 2\sin^2\theta = 0$$

hints: Use the result from part (a) and factor it as a product of two linear expressions in $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$.
Each factor gives a tangent equation: one with $\tan\theta=1$ and one with $\tan\theta=-\frac13$.
Find every solution in $0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$, using the correct quadrant for the negative tangent.
walkthrough:
Factorise the quadratic expression in $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$:
$$\cos^2\theta + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta - 3\sin^2\theta = 0$$
$$(\cos\theta - \sin\theta)(\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta) = 0$$

Set the first factor equal to zero:
$$\cos\theta - \sin\theta = 0 \implies \sin\theta = \cos\theta$$
$$\tan\theta = 1$$

Set the second factor equal to zero:
$$\cos\theta + 3\sin\theta = 0 \implies 3\sin\theta = -\cos\theta$$
$$\tan\theta = -\dfrac{1}{3}$$

Solve for $\theta$ in the second quadrant ($0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$):
$$\theta = 180^\circ - \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 180^\circ - 18.4349^\circ = 161.5651^\circ \approx 161.6^\circ$$

State all solutions in the given interval:
$$\theta = 45^\circ \quad \text{and} \quad \theta = 161.6^\circ$$
